brief.subject: Diesel jumps 7.6 cents; Mexican truckers strike
brief.headline: Diesel climbs to $6.352 as Mexican truckers strike and Motus fix stays undated
brief.dek: Diesel rises week over week, a Mexico strike threatens border freight, and brokers get no quick federal guidance on carrier vetting.
brief.lede: Diesel rose 7.6 cents last week to a $6.352 national average. Recheck your fuel surcharges before booking this week's loads.

sections.heading: Diesel Jumps Again
bullets: $6.352 per gallon: EIA's U.S. average retail diesel for the week of 2026-10-26.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) from the prior week, so make sure fuel surcharges keep pace before booking.
Down 3.0 cents over four weeks, so the jump erased only part of the recent relief.
USPS will add a weekly fuel fee in 2027 tied to diesel and jet fuel, matching FedEx and UPS.

sections.heading: Mexican Truckers Strike Nationwide
bullets: Nationwide strike began Monday, driven by highway security concerns and rising costs.
Protests are planned at major freight hubs and could slow commercial and cross-border traffic.
Border-lane carriers should expect delays and confirm pickup windows with shippers and brokers.

sections.heading: No Carrier-Vetting Rules Coming Soon
bullets: TIA's chief says federal guidance on broker carrier selection is not close.
Brokers sought it after two court decisions this year went against them.
Without clear rules, expect brokers to keep tightening safety and insurance checks on small carriers.

sections.heading: Motus Repair Still Undated
bullets: FMCSA deputy administrator Jesse Elison again addressed the troubled Motus registration system.
No date was given for a full repair, so allow extra time for registration tasks.

sections.heading: CSX Courts Truckload Freight
bullets: CSX is reviewing shippers' truckload files to pitch intermodal service and cost comparisons.
The railroad sees a weak trucking market as an opening, adding pressure on long-haul truckload rates.
